expectations.text: Recognizes that no capability breakdown was provided
expectations.evidence: Line 1: 'Right now I don't have either the capability breakdown or a description of the app, so I'd be inventing both.' Line 3 header: '## 1. I need the capability breakdown first'.

expectations.text: Tries to retrieve the breakdown via the librarian skill, or asks the user to provide it
expectations.evidence: Lines 13-22 '### On retrieving it automatically' explain that normally the librarian skill would be used but 'The librarian skill isn't available in this environment', then ask the user to paste/point to the breakdown (line 9, 22).

expectations.text: Does NOT fabricate a full architecture for an unspecified app without any capability basis
expectations.evidence: No architecture or stack is produced. Line 1: avoids 'inventing both', and line 37 describes the architecture only as what will be produced once inputs arrive.

expectations.text: Asks a small number of targeted questions (not an exhaustive questionnaire)
expectations.evidence: Lines 28-31 list exactly four constraint topics, explicitly framed (line 26) as 'just the handful of questions that genuinely move the architecture, not an exhaustive questionnaire.'

expectations.text: If it asks constraint questions, they focus on high-leverage items (scale, team, hosting, compliance)
expectations.evidence: The four questions are Scale & load (line 28), Team (line 29), Hosting (line 30), and Hard constraints incl. compliance HIPAA/PCI/GDPR/SOC 2 (line 31) — exactly the high-leverage items.

expectations.text: Suggests running the solution-architect skill first if no breakdown exists
expectations.evidence: Line 10: 'If no — that's fine, but I'd strongly recommend running the solution-architect skill first. It will produce a much stronger, more honest architecture than me guessing at the capabilities.'

expectations.text: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
expectations.evidence: Only response.md exists in outputs/; no files written. Line 39 explicitly states 'I don't persist the result myself — saving it is the librarian skill's job.'

expectations.text: Behavior reflects 'build on the breakdown' principle rather than guessing the whole system
expectations.evidence: Line 5: 'Every layer of the stack I recommend gets traced back to a specific capability, so nothing is unsupported and nothing is gratuitous.' Whole response is anchored on obtaining the breakdown before designing.

claims.claim: The librarian skill is not available in this environment
claims.evidence: No librarian calls; assistant degrades to asking the user, consistent with unavailability.

claims.claim: Persisting output is the librarian skill's job, not the architect's
claims.evidence: Line 39 states this explicitly and the assistant does not save any file, matching the 'build on the breakdown' / separation-of-roles design.

workarounds: Librarian skill unavailable; asked user to provide breakdown directly and described how an agent with librarian access could retrieve it

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT attempt to persist/save output
suggestions.reason: Passes trivially in a single-turn ask-first scenario with nothing to save. More discriminating if a breakdown is supplied and an architecture produced, so the no-self-persist behavior is genuinely exercised.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions discriminate genuine 'ask first' behavior from fabrication and are strongly satisfied here. Only the persist assertion is weak in this single-turn context.
